| identity | `required-open` | A motion is first-order data: a list of tracks, each a key, a change of one kind and a transition. An easing is a list of stops or the two heights of a cubic, in per mille. No function is stored. Open: the declaration records of motion: no record names each declaration's owner and anchor yet (debt D125). Discharged: declarations `Whatwg.Svg.Scene.Easing`, `Whatwg.Svg.Scene.Transition`, `Whatwg.Svg.Scene.Pose`, `Whatwg.Svg.Scene.Change`, `Whatwg.Svg.Scene.Track`, `Whatwg.Svg.Scene.Motion` and `Whatwg.Svg.Scene.Plan`. |
| construction | `required-open` | A step's motion is built from the join of two pictures and a plan: what a kept thing does, how a new thing enters and how an old one leaves. A motion is then held in its step, started later thing by thing, put after another, fitted to a length, or reduced to its ends. Open: nothing in the type of a motion says that a thing has one track at most for a property: two shifts on one key are a term. Discharged: declarations `Whatwg.Svg.Scene.Motion.ofJoin`, `Whatwg.Svg.Scene.Motion.staying`, `Whatwg.Svg.Scene.Motion.leaving`, `Whatwg.Svg.Scene.Plan.moving`, `Whatwg.Svg.Scene.Plan.and`, `Whatwg.Svg.Scene.Motion.within`, `Whatwg.Svg.Scene.Motion.delayed`, `Whatwg.Svg.Scene.Motion.andThen`, `Whatwg.Svg.Scene.Motion.fit`, `Whatwg.Svg.Scene.Motion.reduced`, `Whatwg.Svg.Scene.Change.morphOf` and `Whatwg.Svg.Scene.Transition.per`. |
| semantics | `required-open` | `Track.at` is the meaning: the pose of a thing at a moment, by the easing of the share of the duration that has passed, with one rounding down. `Join.drawn` says which things a reader draws at a moment of a step. Open: a moment is a whole thousandth of a step: the reading says nothing of a time between two of them, which a browser draws; the reading gives the poses of a key and not what the thing then looks like: no function of the kit puts the poses on a thing, and two poses of one property have no stated meaning (debt D124). Discharged: declarations `Whatwg.Svg.Scene.mix`, `Whatwg.Svg.Scene.Easing.at`, `Whatwg.Svg.Scene.Easing.of`, `Whatwg.Svg.Scene.Transition.at`, `Whatwg.Svg.Scene.Change.at`, `Whatwg.Svg.Scene.Track.at`, `Whatwg.Svg.Scene.Motion.poses`, `Whatwg.Svg.Scene.Motion.posesOf` and `Whatwg.Svg.Scene.Join.drawn`. |
| laws | `required-open` | The end law: a track whose transition is over stands at the end of its change, so a step's last moment is the next picture, and with a plan that settles every thing of the new list is then at rest. Between the two pictures: a kept edge that changes its shape by its nodes' transition stays joined to them, and a relation of both pictures is a relation of every moment where the things share one timing and the easing stays in range. In time: a delay by depth, a fit to a length and a reduction to the ends each keep the order that the tracks had. Open: a fact of an easing at whole stops does not reach a transition of a duration other than a thousand, and the duration that a distance asks for has no law of order (debt D126); no law says that a thing that leaves ends as nothing: a plan's `leave` may be any change. | representation | `required-open` | An easing of two heights is the curve that CSS names `cubic-bezier(1/3, y1, 2/3, y2)`, whose first coordinate is the progress, and the reading of a transition is that polynomial at the exact share of the duration, rounded down once. A list of stops is what CSS names `linear(…)`. The writer gives each track two keyframes, a duration, a delay and its easing, filled both ways. Open: no law relates the written sheet to the reading: CSS animations, CSS easing functions, the individual transform properties and `d` as a property are not sealed, and the package holds no model of what a browser computes from them; debt D119.
